original_card.question: Can a decoder deliver the local paid mass in fewer, larger-rank children (block frame climbs instead of rank-1 to rank-3 steps)?
methods: Find one exact small decoding identity whose frame path climbs in blocks, and price its complete per-call profile.
Bound the best effective child rank achievable for one fixed support alphabet, including copies, frames and restoration.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A per-call local profile, with all copied information, frames and restoration counted, whose ceiling exceeds the selected word's by at least 5%; masked or overcomplete supports must change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin. Ideal budget: rank-16 delivery is 2.31x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of recursive cost; the selected word's effective child rank is about 3.9. Larger-rank delivery lowers recursive cost per unit of paid mass.
allowed_variations: One masked, overcomplete or block decoder family with exact labels and supports.
A scoped lower bound on effective rank for one alphabet.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Repacking idle remainders of an unchanged word (covered by the packing ceiling).
Repeating the eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.

actual_scope: Exact generalized binary support weights for the eight selected P112 coordinate readers, cross-reader minimum-cut overlaps, and an added-term source-support bound proving no two-total COPY saving through union size 43.
scope_change_reason: The original card seeks a physically priced larger-rank child profile. Nearby open PR1633/PR1671 and discussions 1596/1659 cover obvious rank-shape directions; this is a narrower algebraic search-pruning result in Philipp’s still-open coupled rank-two two-total case. It does not meet the 5% construction gate.
bottleneck_link: A cheaper complex decoder could change the binding complex supplier. This exact support obstruction rules out one small-source route to reducing the separate-total COPY charge, but does not price or improve a supplier.
stop_rule: Stop after all eight P112 coordinate codes, complete RREF subspace census for dimensions 1..8, cross-reader size-24 overlap and triple/four-reader thresholds, 511-functional added-reader span census, union sizes 1..43 bill, one exact full-rank two-total boundary fixture, source pins, failure controls and registered replay. Do not search arbitrary larger complex source unions or claim a full ten-term floor.
evidence: RESULT.json and stdlib verify.py: all eight coordinate codes have generalized support weights 24,36,44,48,52,54,55,56; every coordinate pair shares one minimal 24-cut; three reader rank drops require union at least 40, while all four-reader cuts below 44 are 42 size-40 sets and a fifth needs four more ports; the exact 511-functional span census and source-label count give an added-term charge proving no COPY saving for exact two-total source unions through 43 (with predecessor reductions); exact full-rank coupled fixture first drops two retained ranks at 24 but costs 76.
author: Josie Elliston
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance: prepared by OpenAI Codex (offline session 17: mathematical analysis, exact verifier, controls and writing); reviewed, corrected and published by Claude (Anthropic, session 19). No independent human review.

open_questions.question: Can the remaining full-rank, overlapping two-total P112 case lower the total separate-total COPY sum below 64?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A genuine rank-shape decoder improvement needs the complete two-source tradeoff, including added-term charges.
open_questions.first_step: Use the 24/36/40 support thresholds to prune a source-support-aware exact search beginning at union size 44, retaining the non-free basis dependence of beta.
open_questions.blocked_by: The present theorem proves the complete COPY floor only through source union 43; larger unions may have several retained rank drops and need sharper added-term bounds.

open_questions.question: Are the exact cross-reader support thresholds for four or more rank drops useful to a physically priced decoder?
open_questions.why_it_matters: They could restrict candidate source alphabets or reveal a shared-source pattern.
open_questions.first_step: Enumerate unions of minimal evaluation-code supports with source coefficient constraints, then price all added terms and restoration.
open_questions.blocked_by: The current result proves the triple threshold and the four-reader census only below union 44, and an unconstrained union need not be attainable by two complex source columns.
